_readme: Smart Order nutrition dataset. `verified:true` means every listed item for that chain was checked on this pass against a current official U.S. nutrition/menu source and all macro fields used by the app are populated. `verified:false` means at least one listed item is partial, older-source, imported, or still needs official re-checking. `net_carbs_g` is total carbohydrate minus dietary fiber when both are published. Bump `version` and `updated` whenever you change anything, and make version.json match.
tips: Sauce is the quietest calorie source on the menu. A single dipping cup runs 100–200 cal and 5–10g sugar. Ask for it on the side and use half.
Cheese adds roughly 90–120 cal, 8g fat and 200mg sodium per slice or scoop. It's the single easiest thing to drop.
Fries are almost never worth it here. A medium adds 350–450 cal and turns a reasonable order into a heavy one. A side salad or fruit cup is a 200–400 cal swing.
A medium regular soda is 200–300 cal of pure sugar and doesn't fill you up. Unsweet tea, diet, or water is the biggest single win on the whole order.
Grilled beats crispy every time — usually 150–250 fewer calories and about half the fat for the same protein.
Sodium is the hardest target in fast food. Almost nothing clears 600mg once it has bread, cheese and sauce. Bowls and salads are where you'll find it.
Skipping the bun cuts about 120–200 cal and 25–35g carbs, and most places will serve it in a bowl or lettuce wrap if you ask.

chains.name: Chipotle
tips: Build a bowl, not a burrito. The tortilla alone is about 320 cal and 50g carbs.
Fajita veggies instead of rice keeps the bowl full-sized for almost no calories.
Sodium is the weak spot. Salsas carry 200–550mg each — pick one, not three.

tips: Grilled Nuggets remain the cleanest protein-per-calorie play on the current menu.
The current Cool Wrap is much more calorie-dense than older nutrition datasets show, so do not treat it like a 350-calorie wrap.
Sauces are separate from entrée nutrition and can change the order quickly.

chains.name: Whataburger
tips: The Jr. is the whole trick here. Same sandwich, roughly half of everything.
Grilled chicken looks lean until you check sodium — it's over 1,200mg before you add anything.
Breakfast is the heaviest part of the menu. Taquitos run 380–530 cal each.

chains.name: McDonald's
tips: Nothing on this menu clears 600mg sodium except the plain burgers and the nuggets.
The McDouble is the quiet protein pick — 22g for 390 cal.
Breakfast is the sodium trap. Most biscuits and bagels run 1,100–1,500mg.

items.note: Best breakfast item on the board

tips: The current grilled option is the Grilled Chicken Ranch Wrap, not the older Grilled Chicken Sandwich.
The Jr. burger line keeps portions more manageable than the full-size burgers.
Wendy's current menu still includes the Parmesan Caesar Salad, chili, baked potato and apple side options.

chains.name: In-N-Out Burger
tips: Protein Style is the highest-impact swap here: replacing the bun with lettuce cuts a large chunk of carbs and calories.
If sodium is the priority, the Protein Style Hamburger is the standout among the burgers in this set.
Fries are a full 360 calories, so the burger choice matters less if fries automatically come along for the ride.

items.name: Hamburger — mustard & ketchup instead of spread

chains.name: Shake Shack
tips: A plain single hamburger trims calories versus the ShackBurger, but sodium is still substantial.
Chicken Bites add protein without a bun, though the sodium climbs quickly.
Fries add 470 calories before cheese sauce or a shake enters the chat.

chains.name: Sonic Drive-In
tips: The 2-piece Crispy Tenders are one of the cleaner small orders here at 170 calories and 490mg sodium before sauce.
The Jr. burger line is much easier to fit into a calorie target than the full-size burgers.
Small fries and small tots are still about 250 calories each, so 'small' is doing some emotional labor.

chains.name: Sweetgreen
tips: The Kale Caesar is unusually low in net carbs for a full entrée, but sodium still runs high.
Salads and bowls can look automatically 'healthy' while sauces, grains and crunchy toppings push calories past 600.
Use the nutrition numbers on the complete build, not just the base greens.

chains.name: Culver's
tips: A single ButterBurger is substantially easier to fit than the double.
The Strawberry Fields Salad with grilled chicken is the standout low-net-carb entrée in this set.
Steamed broccoli is a genuinely light side at 40 calories and 40mg sodium.

items.name: Garden Fresco Salad w/ Grilled Chicken
Strawberry Fields Salad w/ Grilled Chicken

chains.name: Noodles & Company
tips: Small portions are the easiest lever here; several small bowls land around 320–430 calories.
The Kids Grilled Chicken Breast with marinara is extremely protein-dense, though it just misses the app's 600mg sodium target.
Noodle dishes can stay moderate in calories while still carrying 1,000mg+ sodium.

items.name: Kids Grilled Chicken Breast w/ Dipping Marinara

chains.name: El Pollo Loco
tips: Ordering chicken pieces or chopped breast gives you far more control than starting with a loaded bowl.
The Double Chicken Avocado Salad is high-protein and low-net-carb before dressing, but sodium is still above the app target.
Broccoli and pinto beans are much lighter side choices than rice-heavy combinations.

chains.name: The Habit Burger Grill
tips: The Charburger is calorie-manageable but very high in sodium.
Crispy Chicken Bites provide solid protein, but sodium rises fast with portion size.
The veggie patty itself is low in calories and under 500mg sodium before the rest of the sandwich is built.

chains.name: Dunkin'
tips: Protein drinks can add meaningful protein, but flavored versions still carry substantial sugar.
Avocado Toast stays under 250 calories; bacon raises both calories and sodium.
This chain remains unverified until the full current U.S. guide is re-opened and all selected rows are rechecked.

chains.name: Panera Bread
tips: Wraps in this sample are protein-forward but generally high in sodium.
Hard-boiled eggs are the low-carb, low-sodium outlier.
The 2026 guide was indexed, but the live file could not be fully re-opened during this pass, so the chain stays unverified.

chains.name: Dairy Queen
tips: The currently accessible official nutrition table is older than this dataset's target freshness, so treat these as recheck-needed.
A 2-piece chicken strip order is far easier to fit than a full basket.
Combos are where calories accelerate fastest because fries and drinks stack on top.

chains.name: Jimmy John's
tips: Little Johns keep calories near 240–340, but sodium still ranges widely.
Turkey-forward choices are leaner than several of the Italian club builds.
The official guide available in this pass is effective July 2024, so it is not marked current-verified.

chains.name: Domino's
tips: Thin crust consistently cuts calories and sodium versus hand-tossed in Domino's official lighter-options examples.
These rows are per 1/8 of a 12-inch pizza, not per whole pizza.
Protein, total fat and net-carb fields remain null until the full build calculator is captured.

chains.name: Raising Cane's
tips: The current official menu publishes calories clearly, but full macro fields were not extractable in this pass.
One chicken finger is 130 calories before sauce.
Cane's Sauce is 190 calories per serving, so dipping can meaningfully change the order.

chains.name: Popeyes
tips: The current wing flavors in this sample are all sodium-heavy.
Full current Blackened Tender nutrition still needs to be captured before Smart Order can confidently surface the chain's best lean-protein choice.
Sauce choice matters as much as wing style once sweet glazes enter the picture.

chains.name: CAVA
tips: CAVA publishes calories on current menu pages, but the complete macro rows still need calculator-level capture.
Treat these as calorie anchors rather than fully scored Smart Order items until protein, sodium and carb fields are filled.
Custom builds can vary dramatically based on dips, dressings and pita.
